page: Microsoft Azure F4ams_v6 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famsv6 server family. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is not included, though the instance is premium storage capable for external disk attachments.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing and small-model LLM text generation also demonstrate strong performance. Multi-core CPU performance, database operations, and Redis SET operations fall within the average range. However, a notable performance tradeoff is observed in memory bandwidth for large uncached read blocks, which registers in the bottom 25% at 38.92 GB/sec, alongside weaker prompt processing speeds for medium-sized LLM models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F4ams_v6 offers a dense memory allocation relative to its 4 dedicated vCPUs, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The hardware profile is suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, text processing, and lightweight LLM inference tasks.
